title: For a smooth complex genus-three (3,4) curve in form (2.4), the second-kind cohomology basis (3.2) with the primitive-sigma normalization has regularization vector (0,-lambda2/3,-lambda5/6) at infinity
author: Julia Bernatska; Dmitry Leykin
source_title: On Regularization of Second Kind Integrals
difficulty_reason: The additive regularization vector is fixed by compatibility with the Abelian-function field and the specified multivalued primitive, not by removing the pole alone. The author derives residue identities and rational-function elimination relations on a nonspecial divisor, then uses a bilinear sigma identity to determine every component uniquely. This supplies the complete geometric and Abelian-function support for the final local coefficient calculation.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The full alternative Proof2 of Theorem4.1 and all its new local support in Lemma4.5 were read, with the exact primitive/sigma normalization and the full chosen cohomology basis. The author derives the second-kind Abel integral relations by residues, differentiates them to obtain rational functions vanishing on the nonspecial divisor, and derives the required Abelian-function identities from elimination and parity. The bilinear sigma/primitive relation then has an explicit Laurent expansion whose coefficients uniquely determine c=(0,-lambda2/3,-lambda5/6). The equality of meromorphic functions is supported by their stated divisor and leading-term comparison. Select this complete second proof; the alternate first proof is not relied upon.

statement_scope: Full genus-three Theorem4.1 with its complete alternative Proof2. Work with a smooth nondegenerate complex curve y^3+x^4+lambda2*y*x^2+lambda5*y*x+lambda6*x^2+lambda8*y+lambda9*x+lambda12=0, the exact first/second-kind differential basis3.2, local parameter x=-xi^-3 at infinity and the multivariate sigma/primitive normalization2.3/3.1. Then c=(0,-lambda2/3,-lambda5/6). No arbitrary cohomology basis, alternate sigma normalization, singular member, other (n,s)-curve variant or addition-formula neighbor is asserted.
